question.worked_solution:
First, recall the associative law

$$
ABC=(AB)C=A(BC).
$$

Notice that $A$ is a $3\times 2$ matrix, $B$ is a $2\times 3$ matrix, and $C$ is a $3\times 1$ matrix. Therefore,

- multiplying $A$ by $B$ gives a $3\times 3$ matrix, which would require finding $9$ entries, while

- multiplying $B$ by $C$ gives a $2\times 1$ matrix, which requires finding $2$ entries.

So, we find the product $BC$ first:

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & -3 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we multiply $A$ by $BC:$

$$
\begin{aligned}ABC & =A(BC) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ -1 & 5 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -15 \\ -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
